verified_claims.claim: Financial institutions must file a Currency Transaction Report (CTR) for cash transactions exceeding $10,000 in one business day (aggregate rule applies).
CTRs must be filed electronically with FinCEN; institutions generally have 15 calendar days after the transaction to file.
The $10,000 CTR threshold is fixed by statute/regulation and has not been inflation-adjusted (GAO and FinCEN have reviewed this).
Structuring — breaking up cash deposits to evade CTR reporting — is prohibited under federal law (31 U.S.C. § 5324).
Social Security and SSI benefits increase 2.8 percent in 2026 (COLA).
On average, Social Security retirement benefits increase by about $56 per month starting January 2026.
Estimated average monthly Social Security benefit for all retired workers: $2,071 after the 2026 COLA (was $2,015).
2026 maximum taxable earnings for Social Security (OASDI): $184,500 (up from $176,100 in 2025).
On May 19, 2026, the White House signed an executive order directing Treasury to propose BSA/customer-due-diligence changes within 90 days — proposals, not live new deposit rules as of May 27.

not_claimed_by_sources: Depositing a normal Social Security direct deposit does NOT by itself trigger a CTR — CTR applies to cash, not ACH/direct deposit.
The May 19, 2026 executive order did NOT change the $10,000 CTR threshold overnight.
This video does not state specific criminal penalties unless quoted from statute — consult an attorney for your situation.
Banks filing a CTR does not mean you committed a crime — CTR is an informational report.
